hypothesis: With V4_PREFILL_CHAIN=1 a prompt chunk's query, attention and wo run on the card and the host's query, attended and wo_a buffers are never read, yet the batched attention zeroes all three on every call: about 37 MB of memset per chunk and layer (128 tokens x 64 heads x 512 floats, twice, plus wo_a's outputs). Profiling the service showed the attention block about 2.5 ms per chunk-layer longer than the sum of its stages, the same in every layer. Zeroing those buffers only when a host path is about to fill or read them leaves every path's inputs as they were, so the outputs are the same bits, and takes that time off the prompt.
model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 architecture, abliterated weights (same shapes), safetensors, native FP8/FP4
command: make -C c -f Makefile.deepseek-v4 deepseek-v4 CUDA=1 DEEPGEMM=1 CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.3 ARCH=native; deepseek_v4 <model> --prompt-file prompt3k.txt --max-tokens 36 --memory-gb 16 with the environment in config; the arms alternate (baseline, trial) three times on one binary; tok_s = 3278 prompt tokens / time_to_first_token from the engine's `timing` line (prompt throughput)

hardware.storage: Samsung 990 PRO 4TB + 980 PRO 2TB NVMe in one LVM volume, ext4, direct aligned reads

config.binary: deepseek_v4 CUDA=1 DEEPGEMM=1 ARCH=native (one binary, the DeepGEMM sm_120a flavour linked in)

quality.method: greedy text identical across the arm's runs and identical to the trial's (md5 of stdout)
